title: My Korean roommate left me a note… 🍰😳 #learnkorean
caption:
먹지 마 = DON'T eat
In Korean, "don't" comes at the very END of the sentence: verb + 지 마.

케이크 (cake) + 먹지 (eat…) + 마 (…don't!)
= 케이크 먹지 마! → "Don't eat the cake!"

먹지 마 → casual (friends, roommates)
먹지 마세요 → polite

Real handwriting looks different from the textbook, so read slowly — but read it ALL. 😅

pinnedComment:
Write a fridge note in Korean with -지 마 👇
Example: 마시지 마! = Don't drink it!
alt: A memo stuck on a white fridge with a red magnet says 케이크 먹지 마! in fast, slanted Korean handwriting. Below the fridge, a hand holds a plate with a whole slice of strawberry cream cake. A pencil copies the note neatly letter by letter under the scribble: 케이크 (red pen: cake), then 먹지 (red pen: eat). The plate is lifted toward the camera and the cake is eaten in two bites until only crumbs and a strawberry stem are left. Then the pencil writes the last letter 마! and a big red DON'T! is stamped under it; 마 is circled in both lines. Labels read how Koreans really write and how textbooks write it, and red lines link the same letters. A front door opens and the empty plate is pulled out of view.
